full_judgment: 16. Mr Mansur Habib further submitted that the appellate Court only reversed the finding of the trial Court in respect of the kabala dated 16-11-70, Ext. 1 (a) of the defendant found to be forged one by the trial Court is not proper finding of reversal as the court of appeal below relied on the averments in paragraph 2 of the plaint which is not a proper one and in this respect the finding of the appellate Court is of an erroneous view, which is liable be to set aside and the trial Court actually has given reasons for saying the deed dated 6-11-70 Ext. 1(a) of the defendants as forged. by saying that the stamp of the said deed dated 16-11-70 has been purchased on 22-3-69, it has been executed on 15-4-70 and it has been placed for registration firstly on 4-7-70 and it was registered on 24-11-70 (under section 75 of the Registration Act vide order dated 16-11-70) and moreover, the ink of executions of the said kabala dated 16-11-70 are different and with those reasons the trial Court came to the correct finding that the aforesaid kabala dated 16-11-70 Ext. 1(a) of the defendants was forged.
